ov: Clever New World monkeys famous for their foraging skills, including using stones to crack open nuts. They are usually dark brown with a cream or off-white area around the neck, and live in groups of 6 to 40.
len: 30–56 cm, with a tail about as long again
rg: Tropical forests of Central America and South America as far south as northern Argentina; Brazil has the most.
df: Omnivores: leaves, flowers, fruit, seeds and sap, plus insects, molluscs, frogs and other small animals.
fx: Capuchins living near water crack crabs and shellfish open with stones.
Young capuchins learn to crack nuts by watching experienced adults, which can take years of practice.
notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-29 (owner: approve all; animals.js updated): The animals.js fact is confirmed: capuchins use stones as hammer and anvil, and the young learn by watching adults.
